subject: Next steps: Hosted vs Dedicated for FastRetail — latency & QPS targets
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fastretail.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@fastretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + recommended path (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we’re aligned:

Summary of ask:
- FastRetail needs inference for personalization & checkout scoring.
- SLA target: p95 model inference latency <= 120 ms (real user-facing) during peak checkout flows.
- Traffic profile you shared: sustained ~950 QPS during daytime peak, short bursts up to ~2.5k QPS for flash sales. Average prompt length ~18 tokens, response tokens ~30.

Initial read / constraints:
- Hosted API can get you running quickly and handle bursts, but sustained 950 QPS with hard p95 <=120 ms is at the edge for shared capacity and may see variability during noisy neighbors or regional outages.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) gives predictable throughput and much tighter tail latency with predictable autoscale/burst rules. It also supports network isolation and custom kernel selection if you move to quantized model builds later.

Our recommended path for FastRetail (based on risk/cost balance):
1) Pilot on Hosted API for 1 week with your real traffic replay (quickbench) to validate prompt distribution and end-to-end p95 numbers. Host the quickbench workload in the us-west region. We already have a lightweight harness (attached) that will replay traffic and produce per-route p50/p95/p99 and token-cost breakdowns.
2) Parallel sizing run: redwood does a Dedicated sizing estimate using your replay results; if quickbench shows sustained p95 <120ms on hosted for ~75% of windows but spikes above during bursts, we recommend moving to Dedicated with a fallback policy (Dedicated primary, Hosted fallback) to cover ephemeral spikes at lower marginal cost.
3) If quickbench shows Hosted won’t meet the p95 target for sustained windows, proceed straight to a 2-week Dedicated pilot (reserved pool + canary routing).

Action items / next steps:
- Alex: send the replay file (or a 24-hour sample) and the prod traffic spreadsheet (I attached an editable template).
- Ben (cc’d): can you prepare a quickbench config with the sample and run a hosted baseline? Aim for a run that includes a 15-minute burst at 2.5k QPS to capture tail behavior.
- Priyom: please prepare a Dedicated pilot cost estimate and a suggested capacity configuration (we’ll need to size on model variant / quantization later).

Attachments: fastretail_prod_qps_latency.xlsx (template), redwood_quickbench_instructions.md (stub)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for a 30-min handoff once Alex shares the sample.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
https://www.redwood.ai

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fastretail.com>

Subject: Re: Quick recap + recommended path (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Thanks Jasmine — that matches our internal read. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 950 QPS is observed for the personalization scoring endpoint across US regions, ~70% of traffic is during a 6-hour peak window. We can route the replay from a single region (us-west) for the initial bench.
- Model: we’re planning to use a 13B open-weight model, quantized to 4-bit in our owned infra; for the pilot we can use the 13B float variant if you prefer. Typical inputs are small (18 tokens); many requests are idempotent so prefix caching should help.
- Key requirement: p95 user-facing inference <= 120 ms. If Dedicated pricing is reasonable for the reserved pool, we’re open to committing.

I’ve attached a 24hr sample trace (anonymized) and filled the prod_qps template. Also attaching our SRE contact (platform@fastretail.com) who may join the sizing call.

Attachments: fastretail_24h_replay.ndjson (stub), fastretail_prod_qps_latency.xlsx

Subject: Re: Quick recap + recommended path (Hosted vs Dedicated) — proposed pilot plan

Alex / Jasmine / Ben — thanks for the notes and sample data. I reviewed the 24hr trace and sketched a conservative pilot plan: 

Pilot proposal (2 weeks):
- Phase A (week 1): Hosted quickbench baseline using your 24h replay (us-west). Deliverable: p50/p95/p99, batching profile, cache-hit delta, and token-cost estimate.
- Phase B (week 2): Dedicated pilot sizing: allocate a reserved pool sized to handle sustained 1k QPS at p95 <=120 ms with headroom for 2.5k burst via autoscale/burst routing. Suggested starting configuration: 4x H100-equivalent GPUs (logical pool), configured with low-latency kernels and prefix/KV cache enabled.
- Routing plan: Dedicated primary for production routes, Hosted fallback that routes overflow to shared capacity with throttling thresholds. Canary: 10% traffic to Dedicated first day, ramp to 100% as metrics look good.

Estimated costs (rough):
- Dedicated pilot (~2 weeks): estimated reserved pilot cost range $18k–$28k depending on exact GPU family and autoscale behavior.
- Hosted baseline run (1 week replay tests): minimal incremental hosted usage charges (covered by PoC credits).

Deliverables and timeline:
- Today: Ben to schedule Hosted quickbench run (ETA: 48 hours).
- +48–72 hours: quickbench results and a Dedicated sizing recommendation.
- After results: we’ll update a short mutual action plan and DocuSign SOW if FastRetail opts for Dedicated pilot.

Attachments: redwood_quickbench_results.pdf (template summary), pilot_sow_template.docx (stub)

If this plan looks good, Jasmine — feel free to send a calendar invite for the quickbench window (we’ll need a 2–3 hour slot to run the accelerated test). Alex — cc’d your SRE; please confirm the replay upload location (or we can set a presigned S3 link).

Thanks — looking forward to getting the numbers.

Best,
